subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Tea Polyphenols and Health
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Tea Polyphenols and Health.

hook.text: Tea leaves are packed with polyphenols—compounds that protect cells, reduce inflammation, and fight oxidative stress.

buildup.text: Green tea is richest in catechins, especially EGCG—one of the most studied antioxidants in nutrition science.

discovery.text: EGCG has shown anti-cancer, anti-inflammatory, and cardiovascular benefits in hundreds of laboratory studies.

twist.text: Lab results don't always translate to real life. The body absorbs only 2–5% of ingested EGCG—most gets broken down.

climax.text: Despite low absorption, populations with high green tea intake consistently show lower cancer and heart disease rates.

punchline.text: Small absorption, big population effects. Tea polyphenols add up over a lifetime.

quiz.question: What is EGCG?
options: A catechin antioxidant abundant in green tea with extensive health research
